material_facts.description: On 2024-01-08 the patient sustained a left arm crush/entrapment injury in industrial machinery, requiring tourniquet application and dismantling of the machine to free the arm.

The patient presented with a complete traumatic near-amputation of the left arm between the shoulder and elbow with complete brachial artery and nerve transection, exposed bone, and massive soft tissue loss, and traumatic shock from blood loss.

Left upper extremity X-ray and CT angiography showed comminuted displaced supracondylar humerus fracture, open segmental forearm/hand fractures, carpal disorganization, and brachial artery disruption.
Patient received emergent resuscitation including 2 units PRBC transfusion and IV fentanyl/fluids for traumatic blood loss prior to surgery.

On 2024-01-08 Dr. Marcus Vance performed an emergent left transhumeral (above-elbow) amputation with ligation of the brachial artery, traction-neurectomy of the median/ulnar/radial nerves, humeral sectioning, and myofascial closure.
Following amputation surgery the patient was admitted to the ICU for postoperative monitoring including drain placement and later removal.
The patient developed severe phantom limb pain (rated up to 8/10) and stump hypersensitivity following the amputation, managed with escalating gabapentin dosing and desensitization therapy.
By mid-2024 the patient was diagnosed with a post-amputation traumatic neuroma of the ulnar/median nerves at the distal stump after failing conservative management of stump hypersensitivity.

On 2024-11-12 Dr. Marcus Vance performed excision of a 1.8 x 1.4 cm neuroma with proximal resection of the median and ulnar nerves and transposition/embedding of the nerve stumps into the triceps muscle.
The patient underwent fitting and calibration of a custom myoelectric transhumeral prosthesis beginning February 2025, including electrode calibration for biceps/triceps control.

The patient underwent an extended physical/occupational therapy course from January 2025 through June 2026 addressing shoulder ROM/strength deficits, myoelectric prosthesis training, and functional use of the prosthetic arm.

The patient had multiple missed/cancelled therapy sessions, including a cancelled PT/OT session in December 2024 and no-show appointments in May and November 2025, with a later lapse attributed to holiday workload and transportation issues.

The patient has permanent loss of the left arm above the elbow requiring myoelectric prosthesis use, with residual shoulder weakness/fatigue and reliance on the prosthesis for grasping and bilateral coordination tasks.
On 2026-06-22 the patient completed his comprehensive rehabilitation program with near-normal left shoulder active range of motion and was discharged to return to modified light/medium duty work.

In 2022 the patient sustained a left shoulder AC joint sprain and mild rotator cuff tendinitis after a motorcycle fall, treated with physical therapy and work restrictions, predating the 2024 amputation injury.
Post-surgical pain was managed with a multi-week course of IV/PCA opioids (fentanyl, hydromorphone) transitioning to oral oxycodone and gabapentin, with continued PRN opioid use into recovery.
Wound cultures were obtained and prophylactic IV antibiotics (Ancef, Cefdinir) were administered post-amputation, suggesting monitoring for surgical site infection risk.
The patient presented with traumatic shock secondary to blood loss requiring transfusion and fluid resuscitation at the time of initial trauma evaluation.
